patients.summary: Construction worker who joins in 2021 with long-standing constipation; colonoscopy shows megacolon. Dysphagia in 2023 leads to a 2024 diagnosis of chronic Chagas disease with megaesophagus, megacolon and cardiomyopathy, managed by GI, cardiology and the practice; a 2026 ED visit for PVCs reaches the chart only as records.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is a 42 y/o man looking for a primary doctor; hasn't had one in a few years, previously went to a walk-in clinic when needed. Has MassHealth (Medicaid), card verified. Main concern is bowel trouble that has gone on a long time. Works construction, prefers early morning slots. Booked new patient appt 3/23 at 7:40. Intake forms emailed.

conditions.label: Chronic constipation
conditions.note: years of hard infrequent stools with bloating

medications.drug: polyethylene glycol 3350 17000 MG Powder for Oral Solution
medications.sig: Mix 17 g in 8 oz of liquid and drink once daily as needed for constipation

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT

42 y/o man, construction laborer, here to set up primary care. Last regular doctor was years ago; since then only walk-in care.

CC: bowels. For as long as he can remember as an adult he has gone 4-6 days between movements, stools hard, lots of bloating and a full feeling by the end of the week. Has tried prunes, coffee, an OTC stimulant laxative here and there. No blood in the stool, no black stools, no vomiting. Appetite fine. Weight steady per pt. Never had a colonoscopy or any GI workup.

PMH: nothing diagnosed. PSH: none. Meds: none regularly. Allergies: no known drug allergies.
FHx: mother died at 58 of heart failure, he says the doctors back home thought it was from an infection that attacks the heart. Father has high BP and type 2 diabetes. One sister with an underactive thyroid.
SHx: grew up in a farming area in Central America, has been in the US many years. Lives alone, rents an apartment. Never smoked, no alcohol, no drugs. Framing and drywall work, long days.

ROS: no chest pain, no shortness of breath, no trouble swallowing, no fevers.

Exam: thin, well-appearing man in no distress. Vitals per flowsheet. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, mildly distended, tympanitic in the left lower quadrant, nontender, no masses, no organomegaly. No hernias. Extremities without edema.

A/P
1. Chronic constipation with bloating, long-standing. No alarm features today but has never been evaluated and the duration is unusual. Start polyethylene glycol 17 g daily, can skip days if loose. Referring to GI for evaluation and colonoscopy.
2. Health maintenance: CMP, CBC, lipids, TSH (constipation), one-time hep C and HIV screen. Tdap today. PHQ-2 negative.

RTC after GI workup, sooner if bleeding, vomiting or unable to pass stool.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mr. Perez, your blood work came back normal, including thyroid, kidneys, blood counts and cholesterol. The hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. GI should be calling you to schedule. Keep using the powder most days and let me know how it goes.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY GROUP
Date of service: 05/12/2021
Referred by: primary care

Thank you for asking us to see Mr. Perez, a 42-year-old man with lifelong-feeling constipation. He describes bowel movements roughly once or twice a week before starting PEG, with hard stool and marked bloating. Since starting PEG 17 g most days he goes every 2-3 days. No hematochezia, melena, or nocturnal symptoms. No dysphagia.

Medications: polyethylene glycol 3350 17 g daily as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol. Works in construction.

Exam: BMI about 21. Abdomen mildly distended and tympanitic, soft, nontender. Rectal: normal tone, no mass, soft brown stool, heme not tested.

Impression: chronic constipation of long duration in a young man without prior evaluation. A structural cause should be excluded.

Plan:
- Colonoscopy with extended bowel prep given his history, scheduled 06/09/2021.
- Continue PEG; add a second dose on days without a movement.

Allergies reviewed: no known drug allergies.

reports.text:
SPECIMENS: A. Colon, random biopsies, right. B. Colon, random biopsies, left.
GROSS: A. Four tan fragments, 0.2-0.4 cm. B. Five tan fragments, 0.2-0.4 cm.
MICROSCOPIC: Colonic mucosa with preserved crypt architecture, no increase in lamina propria inflammation, no thickened subepithelial collagen, no granulomas, no dysplasia.
reports.conclusion: A, B. Colonic mucosa without significant histologic abnormality. Negative for dysplasia and malignancy.

documents.title: Colonoscopy Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY GROUP — ENDOSCOPY UNIT
Procedure date: 06/09/2021
Procedure: colonoscopy with cold forceps biopsies
Indication: chronic constipation, never evaluated
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care
Allergies: NKDA

Prep: fair; extended prep, residual solid stool in the left colon washed and suctioned.

Findings:
- The sigmoid and descending colon are markedly dilated and redundant, with retained stool throughout. Looping required abdominal pressure and position changes.
- The cecum was reached; appendiceal orifice photographed.
- Mucosa normal throughout where seen. No polyps, no mass, no stricture.
- Random biopsies of the right and left colon taken.
- Retroflexion in the rectum unremarkable.

Impression: markedly dilated sigmoid and descending colon (megacolon) with normal mucosa. No polyps.

Recommendations: continue PEG daily, titrate to a soft stool every 1-2 days; adequate fluids, especially on hot work days. Biopsy results to follow. Given no polyps, average-risk screening interval would be 10 years.

Pathology addendum 06/11/2021: random colon biopsies without significant abnormality.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here to go over the colonoscopy. GI found a very dilated, redundant left colon full of stool; lining normal, biopsies normal, no polyps. Going about every other day now with PEG daily, sometimes takes a second capful on Sundays. Bloating better but not gone. Still working full days.

Exam: abdomen soft, mildly distended, nontender.

A/P: Megacolon, cause not identified at this point. Continue PEG daily, okay to double on days without a BM. Call if no BM for more than 4 days, vomiting, or severe pain. Physical in the fall.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL EXAM

Feels well. Bowels every 1-2 days on daily PEG, occasional bloated weekend. Works outdoors all fall. Completed his two-dose COVID series at a pharmacy this spring; wants the booster.

Meds: PEG 17 g daily as needed. NKDA.
SHx unchanged: no tobacco, no alcohol.

Exam: thin, fit. HEENT normal. Neck without thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, mild distension, nontender. Skin without rashes. No edema.

A/P
- Megacolon: stable on PEG.
- Prevention: colonoscopy June 2021 without polyps, counts as his colon screening. Labs in March were all normal, not repeating. Flu and COVID booster today. PHQ-2 0.
- RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fax: polyethylene glycol 3350 powder, MassHealth requires an Rx for coverage. Sent Rx for 527 g bottle x 3 refills per PCP standing plan.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine check. No complaints today. BMs every other day with the powder, some gas. Busy season starting at work.

Vitals as recorded. Abd soft, mildly full, NT. Heart and lungs normal.

Megacolon, stable. Continue PEG. Physical in October.

documents.title: Bowel question
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called from a job site. Three days without a BM during the heat wave, bloated, passing gas, no vomiting, no abdominal pain beyond fullness. Reviewed: take PEG twice today and tomorrow, extra water through the workday, then back to once daily. Call back or come in if no BM in 48 hours, vomiting, or pain. Pt agreed.

documents.title: Callback
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Follow-up call: had two large BMs yesterday, bloating gone. Back to daily dosing.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PHYSICAL

No new problems. Constipation controlled most weeks with PEG; when he forgets for a few days he gets bloated and uncomfortable, then catches up. No bleeding. Eating normally.

Meds: PEG daily. NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: well, thin. Heart RRR, no murmur, no gallop. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, slight distension, nontender. Extremities normal.

A/P
- Megacolon: stable. Reinforced daily dosing rather than catching up.
- Flu and bivalent COVID booster today. PHQ-2 0. Colon screening done 2021. No labs due this year.
- RTC spring.
